newsitem.title: UK: IPE natgas up further in winter, October also busy.
newsitem.headline: IPE natgas up further in winter, October also busy.

text.p: IPE natural gas futures saw prices rise again on Wednesday afternoon as 325 lots traded, mostly in the winter.

The three months making up the first quarter of next year all rose significantly, with the last trades in January and February each done 0.125 pence a therm higher than the settlement level on Tuesday. The two months rose to 18.525 pence and 18.55 pence respectively.
And the Q1 1998 strip was valued at 17.125 on the basis of trades done in each of the three Q1 months at 1303 GMT.
October was also heavily traded, with 150 lots done in several separate deals.

Although no trades were done in any other month, the market was bid and offered in a reasonably tight range in each of the 12 contract months. Front month August was bid at 9.40 pence and offered at 9.65 pence on its final day before rolling.
The market has been erratic so far this week, with 500 lots traded on Tuesday but no deals done at all on Monday.
